# v0.30.1 — upgrade and recall fixes, with turn recovery as an opt-in

v0.30.1 is a patch release on v0.30.0 and the first v0.30.x release train: it carries the fixes that were ready when the train was cut. It prevents a second copy of a saved tool result on the first replay after an upgrade from v0.29.2 when its bare saved-output marker matches, links the reply copies that a cold restart stores after an edit-and-resend, and improves size fitting for `snippets` recall responses. In the tested cases where the host refused a compaction pass, later passes still made progress, and compaction can continue through a long turn on a small context window. It also carries two recovery paths for turns that v0.30.0 could leave only in the host's database: a turn interrupted by a hard kill in a conversation that uses Hermes's legacy rotating compaction, and a Desktop session whose turn failed and that never ended. The first release candidate turned them on by default, and its checks found that, with two LCM-X engines on one conversation, one path can store rows twice and the other can lose a user turn (see **Known issues**). In this release both paths are off by default ([#2698](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2698), picked onto the release branch in [#2699](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2699)), so on those paths LCM-X behaves as v0.30.0 does; one setting turns them on.

Turn recovery uses `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED` (default `false`). The schema version stays 5. This release is v0.30.1-rc4's tree with these notes added (see **Qualification**).

## Changes since v0.30.0

### Restarts and recovery

- **Opt-in: rows that a hard kill leaves in an abandoned compaction child can be recovered.** With Hermes's legacy rotating compaction (`compression.in_place: false`), over ACP on Hermes v0.21.6 to v0.23.1, a restart resumes the conversation's parent session and abandons the compaction child that holds the interrupted turn, so LCM-X was never shown those rows. With the setting on, at the next start of that conversation, a background worker reads that child with the host's own reader and stores the rows LCM-X lacks, only when the child's stored compaction proof covers everything before them. It runs once per process for each bound session and never on a turn. Those turns do not return to the model's view ([#2626](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2626)). It is off by default; `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED=true` turns it on. Its risks and limits are under **Known issues** ([#2624](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2624), [#2632](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2632), picked onto the release branch in [#2671](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2671)).
- **Opt-in: a Desktop session whose turn failed, and that never ended, can be stored.** On Hermes v0.23.1, a turn that fails or is stopped before its reply finishes returns without the per-turn hook, and a Desktop session never gets a session end, so when no later turn completed, LCM-X held none of its rows. With the setting on, at a later session start on the same profile, a background job reads the host's database, read-only, and stores such a session when its last row is the host's failed-turn notice, it is 10 minutes to 7 days old, and LCM-X holds none of its rows. The job runs at most once every 10 minutes for each process, store and home, and never on a turn. With the setting on, when ingest starts a session from its first row, it also runs the same check a bind runs to reconcile against rows another process already stored. This can reduce duplicates, but reconciling can also skip a user turn that starts with a task-list prefix (see **Known issues**, [#2110](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2110) and [#2418](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2418)). Forward only: only failures after the profile's first catch-up job are stored; failures before it, including those after the upgrade while the setting is off, are not. The same setting turns it on; it is off by default. Its risks and limits are under **Known issues** ([#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042), [#2662](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2662), picked onto the release branch in [#2684](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2684)).
- **Reply copies that a cold restart stores after an edit-and-resend are linked.** After an edit-and-resend, a cold restart stores the session's unstamped reply history again. Each copy now carries a `possible_replay_of` link to the stored reply, so the copies are visible instead of silent; nothing is stored or skipped differently. The ingest ledger moving the resume point up from 0 no longer turns this linking off. Pairing those replies within their turn is planned for a later v0.30.x patch ([#2537](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2537)) ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479), [#2529](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2529), picked onto the release branch in [#2664](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2664)).

- **A stored tool result without a tool name can match its replay through the unique call that owns it.** This fixes repeated cold-bind copies when the replay matches the whole store. See Known issues for stores that already have copies and for post-compaction replays.

### Upgrade from v0.29.2

- **The first replay after an upgrade from v0.29.2 no longer stores a tool result a second time when its bare saved-output marker matches.** v0.30.0 listed this under **Known issues**: when v0.29.2 had stored a tool result as a bare saved-output marker, in the host's temp results folder (a file with Windows line ends included) or with a data URI in its preview, the first replay stored the tool call and its result once more. The upgrade replay and the session-end compare now use one rule for a bare marker: it is the same row only when the host's marker text is byte-identical once placeholders are restored and redaction is applied on both sides, with no recovery from the saved file. For such rows the store keeps the marker v0.29.2 stored, not the saved file's content, as it already did for the plain case ([#2521](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2521)). This holds with sensitive-pattern redaction on or off. A result that the host sends as one text part is not covered yet; see **Known issues**. A later replay can still add a copy when the same call ID repeats the marker, as described under **Known issues** ([#2558](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2558), [#2584](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2584) and [#2663](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2663), picked together onto the release branch in [#2674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2674)). The counts and scope of that named limit in `docs/exactly-once-ingest.md` are corrected to match ([#2677](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2677), picked in [#2678](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2678)).

### Ingest

- **Some ingests hold the write lock for less time.** The identity-anchor presence check now returns before any read when it has nothing to check: no tool call or result among its candidates, and no rewritten row to exclude. Both of its outcomes then give the same result, so those reads only lengthened the write-lock hold. On the bench, this step alone cut the probe's median hold from 433 to 392 ms. It is one step of the busy-database work ([#2293](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2293)); the rest is planned for a later v0.30.x patch (see the busy-session item under **Known issues**) ([#2644](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2644), picked onto the release branch in [#2665](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2665)).

- **A lone UTF-16 surrogate in stored, queried or returned text becomes U+FFFD.** Valid text is unchanged. The store also adds a partial index on session ID and tool call ID for tool rows.

### Recall

- **`snippets` recall hits are fitted to the response size cap.** A `snippets` response could pass the 64,000-character response cap once the query echo, provenance and markers around the hits were counted. Hit delivery for `snippets` now budgets the whole response, with snippet windows off or on, skipped reads and extra entries included. A query echo longer than 4,096 characters is cut to its first 4,096 and reported as `query_truncated` when the serialized response would exceed the cap; with snippet windows, that test uses the response without its hits, including its markers. Full hits are then dropped from the end in rank order with `response_cap_truncated`. Session delivery keeps its own budget. Long diagnostics can still push the response over the cap after all hits have been dropped. A per-call limit too large for an integer, such as `1e999`, now falls back to the default instead of raising an error. Responses that already fit, and stored rows, are unchanged. v0.30.0 listed both defects under **Known issues** ([#2620](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2620), ported onto the release branch in [#2670](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2670)).

### Compaction and long sessions

- **Placing a row deep inside a long session takes less time.** The ingest ledger searches windows of at most 256 labels. When it needs more room, it re-spaces the session once. In the reported case, applying the re-spacing took 135 statements for 20,010 labels, down from 40,021.
- **A compaction finishing after a session switch no longer writes its resume point into the next session.** The finishing pass checks its session binding before it writes.
- **A pass that publishes no summary and performs no other real work returns the caller's conversation unchanged.** This avoids rewriting the provider's prompt cache for an unchanged conversation.
- **With `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=on`, the first compaction after a restart can recognise stored messages by host ID before comparing their content.** Recognition needs `on`; the default mode, `shadow`, records host-ID bindings and reads them as evidence, but never skips a row on a host ID alone. A second compaction call from another thread can return a temporary-block signal while a pass is running, and turn telemetry avoids waiting for the store.
- **On hosts without a leading system message, the leaf selector charges a merged summary carrier for the row the summariser actually reads.** This fixes one compaction stall; the notice limit below still applies.
- **Out-of-order tool results are kept and delivered in call order.** A carried user row is also counted when a hidden-only summary nests the summary head and the last-resort trim cuts it in the same pass.
- **Kept rows use the host's current keys after compaction.** This addresses a double prompt-cache rewrite.
- **Long hexadecimal text counts toward the fallback token estimate at two characters per token** when a run contains at least 65 hexadecimal characters, including a letter and a digit, and the input is ASCII. This applies when the tokenizer is unavailable.
- **Compaction can continue through a long turn on a small context window.** On Hermes hosts with the post-tool re-anchor, LCM-X reports when a pass reduces the prompt and clears the host's two post-compaction flags on the next provider response. This lets Hermes re-arm its three-attempt compaction budget during the turn ([#2863](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2863)). The post-tool, idle and cache-edge checks can keep running after the first pass where the host and profile support them ([#2872](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2872)).
- **Rolling back a refused compaction pass prevents the previous summary head from being stored again on replay.** Current Hermes versions can salvage a result that would make the conversation larger by replacing older tool outputs with placeholders, or refuse it. v0.30.0 kept the refused pass's bookkeeping, so the next turn stored the previous summary head once more as a user message. A refused pass is now rolled back at the next turn, compaction call or session end, and a clean shutdown tries to finish a pending rollback before closing the store ([#3001](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3001)). If the refused pass had saved leaves and merged two adjacent plain-text assistant replies that those leaves cover, later passes can reuse the leaves once the refusal is recorded ([#3006](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3006)). Later passes made progress in the tested forced-refusal cases. Continuation after a natural refusal in the default-mode test conversation was unmeasured. See Known issues for the remaining cases.
- **An emergency fit can keep the turn's latest tool result whole.** When the trailing tool result would be shortened, LCM-X can keep it whole if shortening an earlier excerpt brings the prompt within budget. The full results stay stored.

### Testing improved

- **New regression tests** for each fix above: compaction-child recovery and its review cases; the failed-turn catch-up and its ingest check; the restart after an edit-and-resend; the bare-marker identity on stores that v0.29.2 wrote, plus a check that such a replay stores no fewer rows than v0.30.0; and the `snippets` response cap.
- **Real-host test fixes:** three tests that failed on real host builds in v0.30.0's host-suite run, each for a reason in the test, are fixed: one removed the host variables from the rest of the test process, one waited for a log line that ingest no longer writes, and one assumed path filtering hides an editable install. A new guard fails any test that changes an `LCM_REAL_*` variable ([#2636](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2636), [#2637](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2637), [#2638](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2638), [#2660](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2660), picked onto the release branch in [#2666](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2666)).

- **Additional coverage** exercises bounded ledger re-spacing, session-switch timing, no-publication exits and host UID recognition. The release specification adds four live-session rows (D9–D12) and two smoke checks for the first candidate of the next release that runs the full gauntlet.
- **Refused compaction results** are tested at every point that applies a postponed rollback (the next turn, a compaction call and session end), and the pinned traces now cover the refusal state.

## On by default in this release

The recovery paths are off by default. Set `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED=true` to enable both paths, their reads of the host database and the matching check at a session's first ingest. The embedding privacy filter defaults to off. Host UID mode defaults to `shadow`. The replay recognition fast path requires `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=on`. The ingest ledger defaults to `shadow` mode and semantic recall defaults to local embeddings.

## Upgrade

- **Cloud embeddings.** The embedding privacy filter is off by default. Set `LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED=true` to enable it. For cloud providers, the vector identity changes on profiles whose effective embedding privacy policy changes, so those embeddings need to be rebuilt. Summary vectors are refreshed by catch-up. Chunk vectors are refreshed through the consented backfill. Local embeddings are unaffected. Cloud-embedding recall after the privacy-filter change was not re-measured for this release.

- **Host and Python.** As in v0.30.0: Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is required (0.21.5 or newer recommended), with Python 3.11 or newer. When turned on, the compaction-child recovery applies on Hermes v0.21.6 to v0.23.1 and the failed-turn catch-up on Hermes v0.23.1.
- **Installing from the Hermes plugin catalog.** Hermes v0.23.2's install scanner rates v0.30.0's catalog files "caution": a docstring that spelled out a private-key header line reads as an embedded private key. The installer accepts this rating when the installed revision matches the catalog’s reviewed pin. Without that acceptance, the default policy asks for confirmation in an interactive install and stops a non-interactive install. The docstring was reworded for the install scanner in [#2741](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2741). Installs that already run v0.30.0 are not affected.
- **Store schema.** The schema version stays 5, with no new tables or columns. With the setting on, each recovered row carries one metadata entry (`host_row_recovered:<store_id>` or `unended_turn_recovered:<store_id>`) that nothing in the product reads. The failed-turn catch-up also writes one marker per host home (`unended_catchup_since:<hash>`), which sets the time it starts from; the marker survives a rollback and a re-upgrade, and v0.30.0 ignores it.
- **New setting.** `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED` (default `false`). With it off, LCM-X behaves as v0.30.0 does on these paths. Set it to `true` to turn on the compaction-child recovery, the failed-turn catch-up, the check at a session's first ingest and their host reads, with the risks under **Known issues**.
- **From v0.29.2 or older:** read the v0.30.0 upgrade notes first: the ingest ledger, the removed settings, the identity-anchor switch and the rollback limit.
- **Rollback.** Take a SQLite-safe backup first (see `docs/operator-guide.md`). The rollback target is v0.30.0. The schema does not change, and rows that v0.30.1 recovered (with the setting on) stay in the store as ordinary rows. After a rollback, v0.30.0's own behaviour and its **Known issues** apply to that store again, and two items under **Known issues** below still apply to the rows v0.30.1 recovered: a compaction child resumed by its own id is stored again ([#2630](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2630)), and recovered rows can be stored out of order ([#2672](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2672)).
- **If you ran v0.30.1-rc1.** rc1 had both recovery paths on. Rows it recovered or caught up stay in the store as ordinary rows, and the metadata keys it wrote stay unread while the setting is off. When a session that rc1 caught up is resumed, it is reconciled like any restarted session, so the known loss of pasted scaffold-shaped user turns at a restart applies to it ([#2418](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2418)). If you later turn the setting on, the catch-up starts from the time rc1 first ran it, still limited to sessions 10 minutes to 7 days old.
- **If you ran v0.30.0 on a store that v0.29.2 had written.** The copies that v0.30.0 stored on the first replay after that upgrade stay in the store: v0.30.1 does not remove them ([#2558](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2558)).

## Known issues

Four items are named in this release's decision: one unstored reply, one compaction stall, one duplicate and one stored summary head.

- **An assistant reply that calls tools can go unstored when its turn began with two unanswered user messages.** Both must hold: the turn starts with two user messages in a row, which Hermes merges into one before the model call (for example, in a group chat, or when a second message arrives before the agent replies); and the agent's first reply calls tools. LCM-X then counts that reply as already stored without storing it. The reply's tool results are stored, and Hermes's own transcript still holds the reply. Conversation length does not matter. v0.30.0 behaves the same way, and a test reproduces it on v0.30.0, on this release and on main. It was seen at least once on the reference agent. A fix is coming in v0.30.2, and a later release adds a repair that restores such replies from the host transcript. As long as the transcript still holds such a reply, nothing is permanently lost once that repair ships.
- **After a restart, compaction can make no progress on a long conversation at the default setting.** On one of the reference agent's long conversations, ten compaction passes after a cold start freed none of the host's messages, so the conversation kept its size. v0.30.0 behaves the same way. Nothing is lost: every row stays stored. With `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=on`, the same conversation made progress on all ten passes. That test has limits: no pass reached the restart copies themselves, and the host's commit check was not replayed. That mode also has its own restart duplicate, listed below ([#2910](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2910)). The fix is planned for v0.30.3, the release after the first patch release ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **After two compactions inside one turn, the session's first message can be stored twice.** When a session's only user message starts a long tool loop and compaction runs twice inside that turn, the turn's end stores that first message a second time, byte for byte. This was seen on 6 of the 7 tested Hermes versions. Nothing is lost: recall can return the message twice. In the same case v0.30.0 makes no compaction progress, and earlier builds stored the same copy: two of the reference agent's sessions from August show it. Its fix ([#3013](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3013)) is planned after the merged-reply loss fix and [#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674).
- **The summary at the start of the conversation can be stored as a user message.** This was seen on the previous build and in a preliminary comparison on this release too (T1-490, T1-491). A later pass may send the summary twice, once as the summary and once inside that user message. That later pass is still untested. No stored row is lost. This case and the related no-leaf case ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286)) are checked after release (T1-513). A live recurrence on this release or a worse comparison result triggers a same-day patch.

v0.30.2 is reserved for the merged-reply loss fix, the first item above (T1-482). The other planned fixes below come in later v0.30.x patches (T1-517).

Loss limits come first. “Resume point” means the position through which LCM-X believes it has already examined the host’s messages. Rarer shapes that probes found and no real trace shows are listed as named limits in the [Nothing lost: named limits](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/milestone/33) milestone.

### Loss limits

- **A fresh turn that repeats a stored session by content can go unstored on a cold bind even if its host UIDs differ.** The fix missed the cut.
- **A user turn that pastes one of LCM-X's summaries followed by the user's own text can be missing from the store** even though the model saw it on that turn. Two engines sharing one database can also summarise the same leaves twice.
- **Under heavy two-writer contention, a busy session end can leave unsaved messages in memory pending retry.** A process kill or crash before retry can lose that tail. Write-lock work continues in a later v0.30.x patch.
- **Text the host adds to a message that carries a saved-payload marker is not stored.** LCM-X saves a large payload to a file and leaves a marker in the message. If the host later sends the same message with text added before or after the marker, the added text is not stored after a restart: it is in no stored message and in no saved payload. The original message and its payload stay stored. v0.30.0 behaves the same way. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2850](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2850)).
- **A message the host writes into a chat when no turn is running is stored late, or not at all.** The host can mirror a scheduled (cron) delivery into a chat's history between turns. LCM-X receives messages from turn hooks, so it stores that message at the chat's next turn, merged into that turn's first user message. If the chat never has another turn, the message is not stored. Seen once on the reference agent during the v0.30.0 window (1 row pending). v0.30.0 behaves the same way. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2853](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2853)).
- **With `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED=true`, a user turn that starts with a task list can be lost.** Off by default. Only when two LCM-X engines (for example two processes) bind the same empty session and one stores rows before the other's first turn: the check at that first turn then sends it through the restart path, which skips a user message that begins with the task-list header when it sits right after the stored rows, so that message is never stored. v0.30.0 stores it, and stores some of those rows twice. Found in rc1 by a paired engine-level probe. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042), [#2418](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2418)).
- **An interrupted helper agent can lose the rows after its last save.** A helper agent's rows are saved before each of its model calls; the hook waits at most 2 seconds for the save, which then finishes in the background. A save that cannot finish (a database that stays busy, an error) leaves its rows to the helper agent's next save or its end. If the process ends before a save has stored them, the rows since the last stored save are not saved. This happens while its tools run: that round's tool call and finished results stay only in the host's database. It also happens while a save waits more than 5 seconds on a busy database at shutdown, and then one WARNING gives the number of rows not yet saved. Every earlier row is saved for a helper agent that runs its own LCM-X engine, while that engine still serves the profile the helper agent started with. Otherwise, and for a helper agent without its own engine, the rows not yet saved are saved only when the helper agent finishes, so an interruption loses them, as before v0.30.0. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2482](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2482), [#2483](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2483)).
- **New messages after a host-shortened history are lost.** If the host shortens the conversation on its own, such as an undo followed by a compression request that compacts nothing, later new messages are treated as already stored and are not saved. Which hosts produce this shape is not established. A second known route is Hermes's message-sequence repair, which runs only when message alternation is broken and rewrites the list in place: if LCM-X ingests the repaired, shorter list before the next new message, that next user message is not stored. No run has shown this route yet. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1525](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1525)).
- **A re-stamped message can be lost if it arrives while a busy session end's write is pending.** This needs two things: the database is busy at a session end, and the host then shows an earlier message again with a new timestamp before LCM-X's retry runs. In most such cases a later session end stores it, but in two shapes it is never stored. The earlier copy of the same text is kept, and no other row is affected. v0.30.0 behaves the same way. The two shapes are a named limit ([#2778](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2778)).
- **After a restart, one tool-call row can be lost when the host shows the call twice.** This needs three things: the host shows an already stored tool call with a new timestamp, a restarted LCM-X sees it first, and later in the same view the host shows that call again with its original timestamp and no result yet. The store then keeps one copy of the call instead of two, and if that copy's result arrives later, the result is stored without its call row. No real host trace shows this sequence yet. v0.30.0 behaves the same way. The fix is planned for a later v0.30.x patch ([#2782](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2782)).
- **A tool call can stay unstored when its result is already stored.** If a tool call below the resume point is unstored while its result, at or past the resume point, is already stored, the call can be counted as stored without being stored. The result is kept. A repair planned for v0.30.3 can restore such calls while Hermes's transcript still holds them ([#3022](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3022)).
- **Repeated text is under-stored on partial-history hosts.** After a restart and compaction, a host that sends only new messages loses occurrences of text repeated within the session. The reference agent sends full history. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124)).
- **Repeated compacted-out tool pairs are lost.** On hosts that reuse tool-call IDs, a new call and result identical to a pair compacted out of view are treated as a replay after a cold restart and are not stored. The already-shipped fix for a pair still in view does not cover this shape. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **Busy session end with undo and resend leaves a message unstored.** With ignore patterns configured, a busy session end followed by undo, resend and an ingest that changes nothing leaves the earlier occurrence pending and counted at exit, but not stored ([#2247](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2247)). Separately, without ignore patterns, any busy session end followed by an undo and resend also keeps the earlier occurrence pending, counted and reported at exit rather than stored. Only a host resume of that session recovers it; `/new` does not. ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838), [#2206](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2206)). Planned fix: v0.30.x.
- **An ignored-message placeholder makes a later loss silent.** If ignore patterns are or were configured and the session-end view contains an LCM-X ignored-message placeholder, a busy session end followed by undo and resend loses the earlier occurrence. Session end logs a pending retry, but the later drop is neither counted nor reported. v0.29.x lost the same message on this trigger but warned at session end that final messages might be missing; v0.30.0 no longer gives that warning. No ignore patterns are set by default. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2474](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2474)).
- **Untimestamped replacements before the resume point are lost.** A host merge or replacement before the resume point drops an unstamped new row; if an entirely unstamped view replaces all rows at the same length, none of the new rows is stored. On Hermes this follows undoing every turn or retrying a one-turn session when no host database exists or its transcript write failed; timestamped rows are stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#7](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/7)).
- **Some moved tool rows are still skipped.** A moved tool call or result before the resume point is not rescued when the audit finds no missing row there. The audit never examines tool rows on its own: a tool call and result replaced before the resume point are lost, and a pair inserted there stores its result without its call ([#2452](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2452)). Tool groups that cross the resume point while their unstamped results were already stored also retain the old skip behaviour. Affected new rows are not stored; planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467); fixed in v0.30.0 on turns where the audit also misses a row inside the presence window, [#2455](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2455)).
- **Large or non-standard tool histories keep the old loss behaviour.** The moved-tool check does not run beyond 10,000 stored rows, 15 million bytes of stored text or 10,000 tool-call entries across the session and its ancestry. It also falls back for the whole scope if any stored tool-call format is non-standard: call entries must be objects with text IDs and text arguments. New moved rows left classified as positional replays are not stored, and one INFO line reports the limit; planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467); fixed in v0.30.0 on turns where the audit also misses a row inside the presence window, [#2455](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2455)).
- **Externalized arguments and reused IDs bypass the moved-tool fix.** A call whose arguments are externalized at ingest reads as a reused ID, including an inline data URI with at least 256 base64 characters, a run of at least 4,096 base64-alphabet characters, or line-wrapped base64. Reused IDs, repeated call or result IDs in the view, and argument comparisons beyond the 256,000-byte parsing budget retain the old replay decision, leaving affected new call or result rows unstored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172), [#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Replaced unstamped replies and scaffold-looking replies are lost.** If a reply reaches LCM-X without its host timestamp and the host replaces it before the resume point (an edit-and-resend in a long session), the replacement is not stored while the session runs. A restart stores it, together with copies of the session's other unstamped replies ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479)). Replies that carry their host timestamp, as Hermes sends them unless a session has no host database or a transcript write failed, are stored. Planned fix for this part: v0.30.x ([#2116](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2116)). A reply carrying `CONTEXT SUMMARY` markers is still treated as LCM-X scaffold while the engine is running, and lossy-redacted rows still count as replays. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Unreadable ancestry limits moved-row recovery.** If presence reads fail, ancestry cannot be verified with `state.db` present, or a rotation-predecessor write failed in the current process, only rows found by the existing audit are stored. Other rows before the resume point remain classified as replays and affected new rows are not stored; a warning reports the fallback. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Identifier-only replacements behind a merged summary are lost.** When the host changes only a message’s unique ID behind an unchanged merged scaffold, the cached prefix consumes the proof and the replacement is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1428](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1428)).
- **A new occurrence at an alternate timestamp is lost.** Once the original host view is gone, a new event with identical content at a previously recorded alternate timestamp is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1519](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1519)).
- **Earlier edits inside a shortened view are lost.** If a host shortens its view and edits an earlier row in place, LCM-X does not store that edit. This also occurs in v0.27.0. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1563](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1563)).
- **A retried result with only a new ID is lost.** After a cold restart, a retried tool result whose only change is its unique message ID is dropped. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837)).
- **Identical new tool pairs after restart are lost.** A new call and result identical to an earlier stored pair are treated as a replay after restart and are not stored. If the restart follows a stored rewrite of the earlier result, the old call is also stored again beside that rewritten result without a replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2377](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2377), [#2414](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2414)).
- **Pasted scaffold-shaped user turns are lost.** A user turn that starts with the preserved-objective prefix or quotes a whole summary part is skipped when there is no current version-4 compaction proof, including before any compaction, under older proofs or after a cold rebind retires a stale proof. A task-list-prefix turn is affected in every proof state; before any compaction, such turns are skipped after restart even at the tail, or while running when before a stored row. From v0.30.1 the task-list case also reaches an engine that bound on an empty store after another writer stored the session's rows (the catch-up path of [#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042), below), which now reconciles as a restart does; that includes a host composite that carries the user's question. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2110](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2110), [#2418](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2418)).
- **Equal user identities hide a new occurrence.** In a delegated helper agent's session with many equal user messages, after a restart, a failed compaction step or a host head rewrite, a recorded boundary that becomes ambiguous on the next view lets an older copy count against a new one. One occurrence is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2422](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2422)).
- **A warm view that starts with a tool call can store nothing.** When a warm ingest gets a view that starts with a tool call and does not extend the previous view, none of its rows is stored. No host path is known to produce this view. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2419](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2419)).
- **Non-busy pre-compaction write failures lose child rows.** When a delegated child’s input write fails for a reason other than a locked or busy database, such as a disk or I/O error, compaction still removes rows from its view and those raw rows are lost. Their stored summary is the only trace, and `compression boundary not recorded: input not stored` warns about the failure. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2440](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2440)).
- **Multiple timestamp conflicts after busy session end lose messages.** After a busy session end with no later ingest, two or more messages whose host timestamps conflict with saved copies can be lost. If a later ingest brings the same messages unchanged, they are kept and counted instead. v0.29.2 has the same limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x.
- **A same-second resend under a new platform ID is lost.** After a cold restart, a new turn with the same text in the same second as an earlier one, under a new platform ID, is taken as the earlier turn and is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1037](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1037)).
- **A repeated tool step after a rewind can be missed, with an identical message after it.** After a restart, if a conversation was rewound and the agent repeats exactly the same tool call with the same result, followed by a message identical to an earlier saved one, all three are taken as a replay and are not saved, even when the host's timestamps show they are new. We know of no way to trigger this from Hermes today. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2259](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2259)).
- **One half of a re-dated tool pair can be saved without the other.** After a restart in a conversation that LCM-X has compacted, if the host re-dates only one half of a saved tool call and its result as new, that half is saved and its partner is not. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2191](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2191)).
- **Messages pending at a busy session end are missing after a gateway stop until you resume.** If a session end found the database busy and the gateway stops before a retry succeeds, the messages still pending are missing from the store until you resume that conversation. After /new they are not recovered. The only sign is the warning logged when the session ended. The fix needs a change in Hermes ([#2253](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2253)).
- **Messages can be missing if the database stays busy from a session end until the process ends.** If the database is busy when a session ends, stays busy at every later retry (the next session start or end, a related session's start, and the 5-second shutdown drain), and the process then dies or exits while it is still busy, the session's last messages are not saved. They are saved only if you resume that conversation; /new does not recover them. Every busy session end and every failed retry is logged and counted. This is an accepted limit; fixing it needs a journal outside the database.
- **A few restart cases keep messages pending instead of saving them.** After a busy session end, LCM-X keeps a conversation's newest messages pending, rather than risk saving them in the wrong place, in three more cases: a single message that the host re-dates newer than its saved copy; a view rewritten after later messages were saved; and, when the session's binding is ignored or stateless, a message with a different known timestamp. Pending messages are counted and reported at engine shutdown or a normal exit (not after a gateway stop; see [#2253](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2253)), but they are saved only if you resume that conversation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838)).
- **An identical message re-sent in place is taken as a replay.** On hosts that send no message IDs or timestamps, a message re-sent with exactly the same text in the same place, so the conversation does not get longer, cannot be told apart from a replay, and it is not saved again. The same holds when a shortened conversation grows back with identical messages, and for identical overlapping messages in a migration or a full-history replay. This is a design limit: telling them apart needs message IDs or timestamps from the host.
- **Earlier user messages merged into the current turn are not stored.** When a user sends more than one message before the agent replies, for example after an interrupted turn, Hermes merges them into one message for the model. On hosts whose persist step then keeps only the newest message's text (Hermes 0.21.3 as measured, and Hermes's main branch by its code), LCM-X stores only that newest message. The earlier text is stored only if a restart replays the host's transcript. v0.30.0 and earlier releases behave the same way; this was not listed before ([#2707](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2707)).
- **Some Desktop sessions whose turn failed can end with nothing saved.** By default, as in v0.30.0, a Desktop session whose turn failed or was stopped, and that never ended, keeps its rows only in the host's database. With `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED=true`, v0.30.1 stores such a session at a later session start on the same profile (see **Changes since v0.30.0**), within these limits. A session whose failure is older than the profile's first catch-up after the upgrade is not stored; a repair command is planned ([#2652](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2652)). A failed session with no later session start on its profile within 7 days, or with more than 500 rows, also stays only in the host's database. The catch-up stores nothing for a session that has a parent (a delegated, fork or compaction child), that a subagent ran, that ended by compaction, that matches the ignore or stateless session patterns, that holds a row the host has compacted or marked inactive, or whose rows fail its checks: a row with a role other than user, assistant or tool (a `session_meta` or `system` row included), a malformed or empty list of tool calls, a tool call without an id or with an id repeated in its own batch, a tool result without its call or answered twice, a tool call left unanswered, an ignored message, or a last row that is not the assistant's failed-turn notice. It also skips a session in which LCM-X already holds rows, so a failed last turn after stored turns, with no later turn and no session end, stays only in the host's database ([#2693](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2693)). It retries later, while the session stays eligible, a session that this process has bound, that the host changes while it reads it, or whose read or store fails. Each job reads at most the 64 newest candidate sessions and stores at most 16 of them; the rest wait for a later job, and on a profile with more than 64 such sessions within 7 days, the older ones are not read ([#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042)).
- **A first turn stopped during a tool round is not stored** in a session that never continues or ends: the host leaves no failed-turn notice for it, so the catch-up does not pick it up. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2653](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2653)).
- **The last rows of a session can be lost when its end is not written at once.** When a session ends while another session is the active one, or while the store is busy, LCM-X stores its last rows only if the rows it already holds match what the host sends. They do not match if the host changed an earlier message of that session. An earlier row that holds an inline encoded block (line-wrapped base64, or a data URI, inside a tool call's arguments or inside list-form content) can also fail that comparison, even when the host re-sends it unchanged, because LCM-X moved the block out at ingest. The rows after that point, usually the final reply, are then not stored. When another session was the active one, no warning is logged; at most an INFO line says the session was skipped. When the store was busy, LCM-X warns that the end is queued for a retry, warns once more when the retry finds the mismatch, keeps the rows pending, and counts and reports them as not stored at a normal exit. This also occurs in v0.29.2, which in addition can lose the final reply when the store is busy at a session's end, even without such a block. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2543](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2543)).
- **After a restart or a profile rebind, the last rows of a session that ends while another is active can be lost.** When a session that is not the active one ends, LCM-X recognises it by what it recorded about that session in memory, and stores the rows that arrive with the end that it does not yet hold, usually the final reply. A restart, or a rebind of the engine to another profile and back, clears that record, so the end is taken as stale: LCM-X logs one warning ("ignored unverified stale session-end callback") and stores nothing. The rows are stored only if that session is resumed and ingested later. It needs rows that LCM-X did not yet hold at the end: a final reply that only the end carries, or a turn whose save failed because the store was busy. v0.30.0 behaves the same. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2729](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2729)).
- **A busy final save whose undo also fails can lose a session's last rows.** If the save at session end hits a busy database and rolling it back also fails, the last rows are neither stored nor kept for a retry. A later resume of the same session with its full history stores them. Seen only with injected faults; no natural trigger is known. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2736](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2736)).
- **A Ctrl+C during the final save at exit can lose a session's last rows.** An interrupt that lands while the session-end save runs leaves those rows unstored and uncounted; a warning says final messages may be absent. A later resume of the same session with its full history stores them. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2737](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2737)).
- **A busy database at the end of a session that also ran as an ignored session can lose its last rows.** With stateless or ignore session patterns configured, a session id used both ways whose end arrives while another session is active, and finds the database locked for its final append, stores nothing and keeps nothing for a retry. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2738](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2738)).
- **Undoing the tool-output backfill while the profile still runs can delete a saved result that a new row uses.** The optional backfill script writes large historical tool results to payload files, and its rollback deletes the files it created that no row references. The rollback reads which files are referenced once, at its start. If the running profile receives the same tool result again in between (same content, call ID and session), LCM-X reuses the existing file for the new row, and the rollback then deletes it, so that row's content is gone. The operator guide already says to stop the profile before a backfill or a rollback; this happens only when that step is skipped. v0.30.0 behaves the same. Tracked in [#2730](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2730).
- **A saved tool result replaced in place keeps its first content.** If a host replaced a large tool result in place, under the same call ID and with the same size and opening text, LCM-X keeps the content it stored first and does not store the new content. For a session that ended while another was active this is the same as v0.29.2. It also applies to the rows of a delegated helper agent, which v0.30.0 stores for the first time. No supported Hermes path is known to replace a result this way, from a reading of Hermes's tool-result storage code ([#2544](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2544)).
- **A turn with a tool call nested about 2,000 levels deep is not stored.** If a tool call's arguments are JSON nested about twice Python's recursion limit deep (2,000 levels with the default limit of 1,000), LCM-X fails while reading them. No row of that turn is stored, and no later turn is stored while that call stays in the history the host sends. For a delegated helper agent no row of that handover is stored, and none of any later handover that still holds the call; rows from earlier handovers stay stored. The host sees no error; the only trace is a warning in the log. No real tool call is known to nest this deep, but nothing prevents one. This needs Python 3.12 or later; on Python 3.11 the arguments stay unparsed text and the turn is stored. The main-session case also occurs in v0.29.2. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2583](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2583)).
- **When a host replaces an unanswered tool call under the same call ID, a new call that differs only in how a number is written is taken as the stored call.** LCM-X can store a tool call at the start of a turn, before its result exists. If the host then sends that turn again with a call under the same ID whose arguments differ from the stored ones only in the spelling of a number, and both spellings read as the same 64-bit float, LCM-X keeps the stored call, does not store the new call's row, and stores its result. That is intended for one number written two ways (1.0 and 1.00). It also happens for two different numbers that read as one float: 0.1 and 0.10000000000000001, or 1e400 and 2e400. v0.29.2 stores neither the new call nor its result in this case. No supported Hermes version is known to replace a call under the same ID. Planned fix: v0.30.x, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **With payload externalization turned off, a saved tool result is not recognised as the stored row.** This needs a non-default setting (`LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_EXTERNALIZATION_ENABLED=false`). LCM-X then stores the marker of a saved tool result with lines of its own added, and that row never matches the marker the host sends again, so the saved-result matching of v0.30.0 does not apply. When such a session ends while another session is the active one, or while the store is busy, the rows after that result, usually the final reply, are not stored. v0.29.2 loses the same rows with this setting. In a delegated helper agent's session the result is also still stored again on each model call, with nothing marking the copies. Keep payload externalization on, as it is by default. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2547](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2547)).
- **With redaction on, a result saved in the system temp folder can cost a session its last rows.** Sensitive-pattern redaction is off by default. With it on, when the preview of a tool result that Hermes saved in the system temp folder holds text that redaction rewrites, LCM-X cannot pair the stored row with the marker Hermes sends again. If that session ends while another session is the active one, the rows that arrive with its end, usually the final reply, are not stored. v0.29.2 does the same. Hermes saved results there only up to 0.20.4, and LCM-X supports Hermes 0.21.3 and later, so no supported setup is affected; a result saved under Hermes's home is not affected ([#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604)).
- **A hard kill in the middle of a turn can leave that turn's rows only in the host's database.** Only in a conversation that has a compaction child (Hermes's legacy rotating compaction, `compression.in_place: false`; the default is in-place compaction), over ACP on Hermes v0.21.6 to v0.23.1. By default, as in v0.30.0, those rows are not recovered. With `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED=true`, v0.30.1 recovers them at the next start of that conversation, only under a strict proof (see **Changes since v0.30.0**). A conversation that is never loaded again keeps them only in the host's database, on any host and in any mode. A compaction child whose stored proof does not strictly cover the rows before them stores nothing, logs one warning per process and is read again only after a restart: a process reads each bound session's child once, so starting the conversation again in the same process does not retry it; one whose remaining rows hold an ignored row, an orphaned tool result or a damaged tool group also stores nothing. Rows the host's own reader does not return are not recovered, and rows it rewrites are stored as it returns them. A compaction child that LCM-X never bound, and hosts and transports other than the tested ones, are not covered ([#2624](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2624)).
- **A rare message loss after two compactions in a row is under investigation** ([#2330](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2330)): in one run of the reliability test matrix, two messages that arrived right after a compaction rotated the session were never stored, because a second compaction ran in the new session before the turn ended. It has not been reproduced: the failing cell was repeated 8 times on the same host with full logging, and all 8 passed. v0.29.2's notes list the same lead. If it recurs, that run's stores and logs are kept for the fix, which ships in a later release.
- **A hook-only delegated child can rebind its parent's engine.** This is traced in the source only: it has never been observed, and no test covers it yet. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2066](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2066)).
- **A store that a v0.30.0 release candidate wrote can still lose a session's last rows.** A row that a candidate stored while its payload file could not be written, or with redaction on, keeps that form, and a session that holds it can lose its last rows when it ends while another session is active; an early candidate's session can be missing its last rows for good. See **Upgrade** in the v0.30.0 notes. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604)).

These loss shapes are also tracked, each in its own issue:

- **A new user turn that starts with a summary prefix is skipped.** LCM-X takes it for its own summary carrier and does not store it ([#1003](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1003)).
- **Rows appended after a shorter host view are not stored when they carry no host timestamps.** The fix needs the next-stage message classifier ([#1547](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1547), [#2058](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2058)).
- **A host startup stall past the 10 s deadline leaves LCM-X inactive.** No session in that host process is stored until the host restarts or the plugin is reloaded ([#2339](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2339)).
- **On an upgraded store with blank conversation IDs, a legacy row lets another conversation claim its receipt** ([#2423](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2423)).
- **In a session shared by two conversations, a new tool row is not stored** ([#2442](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2442)).
- **Rewrite-memory eviction after 16 notes can lose a merged prompt.** No supported path to 16 notes has been found ([#2476](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2476)).
- **Three routes can send rows to the wrong store if two profiles share one module copy.** Hermes loads one copy per home ([#2499](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2499)).
- **A host that edited a handed-over message in place could have the original skipped.** The ledger binds a digest taken before its transaction. No host writer is known to do this ([#2500](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2500)).
- **A cross-room /resume leaves the fold or snapshot owned by the old conversation** ([#2501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2501)).

### Compaction and long turns

- **A compaction pass can return a larger conversation in every UID mode.** The host can replace older tool outputs with placeholders to make it fit, or refuse the pass and keep the original conversation ([#2982](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2982)).
- **Compaction can still stall after Hermes refuses a pass that saved leaves.** Replies separated by tool rows, merges of three or more replies, and merges whose middle reply was removed by cleanup can still prevent later passes from matching the remaining conversation to their stored sources. Compaction can stall until the emergency cut removes the oldest turns from the model's view, including turns that have yet to be summarised. Those turns stay stored and can be recalled, and the prompt may take several more passes to shrink. The fix is planned for a later v0.30.x patch ([#3006](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3006)).
- **A conversation without a leading system message can lose rows from the model's view during a last-resort trim without a notice.** The rows stay stored and later compaction can cover them. A hidden-only pass can also defer showing a stored summary.
- **A forced pass can remove a tool call with wrapped base64 arguments and its result from view without a summary naming them.** Both rows remain stored. The fix moves to a later v0.30.x patch alongside the remaining copy-set work ([#2890](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2890)).
- **A compaction pass on a very large context window with a slow summary route can use the turn's whole time budget and publish no summary, so the prompt does not shrink on that turn.** Context windows over 480,000 tokens use the existing summary-prefix target. The larger target moves to a later v0.30.x patch ([#2869](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2869)).
- **With more than 100 summaries at one depth, older summaries can leave the view without a pointer when condensation stalls.** The rows stay stored and searchable. A fix was held back after it increased compaction frequency in testing.
- **The summary-prefix budget can drop summaries from view without a notice.**
- **On slow summary routes, prompt growth can continue through a 600-second no-progress hold and later rows can leave the view behind a notice.** The summary-area tidy-up can also run out of budget on each pass. Small context windows can land close to the trigger after a pass.
- **A trim-only pass can report `noop` even when the host rewrites its cache.** The first returned message can also change when survival-fit counts or process-state wording change, triggering another cache rewrite.
- When consecutive emergency fits try to meet the prompt budget, the same earlier tool result can appear with different excerpt lengths ([#3013](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3013)).
- During an emergency fit, the turn's latest tool result can still be excerpted first if it is the largest ([#3013](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3013)).
- **Re-spacing still costs more as a session grows.** The reported application time was about 0.3 seconds at 25,000 rows. A busy thread can still lengthen the first compaction after restart on a large store.
- **Overlapping compaction calls can cause one extra or one missed re-check.** An auxiliary pass on the same engine can overwrite the foreground pass's progress report before Hermes reads it ([#2918](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2918)).
- **A partial summary deletion at /new leaves stored rows that no summary covers.** This is summary coverage, not a stored-row loss: the rows stay stored ([#2045](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2045)).
- **Rotation mapping can stall compaction.** A rotation leaves rows without the mapping compaction needs, so compaction stops making progress. A cold resend after a held fit-only rotation also stores predecessor rows again; those copies now carry `possible_replay_of` links across the recorded rotation chain, except the re-emitted summary marker. Planned fix for the remaining mapping and store-growth limits: v0.30.x ([#2029](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2029)).
- **Turns can drop out of the prompt after rejected summaries.** If two summaries in a row are rejected and the maintenance sweep runs out of time, compaction pauses for 600 seconds. While it pauses, turns that no summary covers yet can drop out of the model's prompt, and the end of the pause does not bring them back. They stay stored, and recall can still reach them. Fix release not yet set ([#2272](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2272)).
- **After a host restart, turns since the first compaction drop out of the model's view.** Only in a conversation that has a compaction child (Hermes's legacy rotating compaction, `compression.in_place: false`, now or earlier; the default in-place mode creates none): on Hermes v0.21.6 to v0.23.1 over ACP (by our reading of the source; not run on a release; seen on two pinned upstream builds), any restart of the host, clean or after a crash, resumes the conversation as it was before its first compaction. Turns since then are no longer sent to the model, and default recall (scoped to the current session) does not reach their raw rows. Their rows remain in LCM-X's store, except the rows of a turn interrupted by a hard kill, which are recovered at the next start of the conversation only with `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED=true` (#2624). This is a host defect, tracked upstream in NousResearch/hermes-agent#148047; v0.29.2 behaves the same. The #2624 recovery does not bring those turns back into the model's view, so this stays open ([#2626](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2626)).
- **A tool call's stored arguments can stop being valid JSON after a long base64 run.** When a tool call's arguments hold a long base64 run right after a `\n` escape, ingest moves the run to a payload file and takes the escape's letter with it, so the stored arguments are no longer valid JSON; ingest can also rewrite a JSON value held as text inside the arguments in compact form. Nothing is lost: expanding the placeholder gives back the original text. If compaction later puts that stored call back into the prompt (only when its arguments are 1,200 characters or fewer), Hermes replaces them with an empty object and logs a warning, so the model sees that one past call without its arguments. Fix release not yet set ([#2792](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2792)).
- **During a no-progress hold, the returned list can skip tool-pair repair.** A kept row can also retain cached content when its replay identity does not reflect a content change.

### Restarts and replay

- **Switching back to LCM-X after Hermes prunes tool results carries a duplicate risk.** From Hermes v0.23.3, the built-in compressor can prune eligible old tool results after the provider cache expires. If it prunes those results before you switch back to LCM-X, replay could store the affected turns’ tool calls again. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2844](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2844)).
- **A refused compaction can still leave one duplicate summary row after a restart.** Shutdown tries the pending rollback for at most the 50 ms session-end busy timeout and skips it if the store stays busy that long or a compaction is still running when shutdown stops waiting. A crash, a host exit without a clean shutdown, or a rebind after busy session ends can also leave it pending. The next turn can then store the previous summary head once more as a user message, and compaction can stall until the emergency cut. The original rows stay stored. The fix is planned for a later v0.30.x patch ([#3001](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3001)).
- **After a restart, a pruned tool result can cause the next session end to store its assistant call again.** This happens in every UID mode. The original row remains stored. The fix is planned for a later v0.30.x patch ([#2781](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2781)).
- **With `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=on`, a cold bind can store known rows again.** One rehearsal on a long conversation recorded eight extra rows with the same count as the comparison build. The original rows remain stored. The fix is planned for a later v0.30.x patch ([#2910](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2910)).
- **A cold reopen can store a placeholder again** when a pruned tool row's placeholder alias declines in the content-only path.
- **Stores that already contain name-only tool-result copy sets can continue adding copies at a cold bind.** The whole-store fallback also misses narrower post-compaction replays. Existing copies are retained.
- **A gateway cold bind can store old tool results and replies again if a backing file is gone.** Independently, three sources of unstamped rows can be stored again.
- **After a re-stamped message and a busy session end, a later clean session end can store the re-stamped row a second time.** Nothing is lost: the extra row repeats the same text. v0.30.0 behaves the same way. This is a named limit ([#2751](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2751)); a first fix was parked after review found further duplicate shapes.
- **With `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED=true`, recovered rows can be stored twice.** Off by default. Only when another LCM-X engine (for example a second process) is still bound to the compaction child that recovery reads, and the host does not stamp its rows, the identity anchor is off (`LCM_IDENTITY_ANCHOR=0`), the identity pre-match fails, or the host rewrites one of those rows in between: that engine's next turn stores the recovered rows again. Nothing is lost. Found in rc1 by an engine-level probe. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2624](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2624)).
- **Two engines bound to the same empty session can store its rows twice.** By default, as in v0.30.0: when two LCM-X engines (for example two processes) bind the same empty session and one stores rows before the other's first turn, the other stores those rows again. Nothing is lost. With `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED=true`, a check at that first turn stores fewer of these copies, but brings the task-list risk listed above. Shown by a paired engine-level probe. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042)).
- **Failed pre-compaction storage also duplicates a head.** After a failed input write before compaction, LCM-X stores the compacted head once more without a replay relation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2440](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2440)).
- **Repeated recovery stores a user row again.** Two recovery fits of a repeated user turn followed by a restart store the projected user row once more, without a replay relation. Fix release not yet set ([#503](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/503)).
- **A later child restart stores kept rows again.** After rejecting a delegated child’s last-stored-row resume boundary, an identical rewritten view stores kept rows again without a replay relation. This takes one restart after a warm rejection or a second restart after a cold rejection; delegated-child restart resume is not reachable on the current host. The record of a child's last compaction outputs is also kept only in memory, so a restart of a delegated child stores its compacted head one extra time. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2439](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2439)).
- **Routing-key changes store the history again.** If the host assigns a live session a new routing key, such as a CLI handoff or resume from another room, the next warm turn stores the whole history again under the new conversation ID without replay relations. This was found in clone-run preflight and code reading and is not yet reproduced on main. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2461](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2461)).
- **Missing compression ancestry duplicates carried rows.** When a compression child’s ancestry cannot be verified and the host inserts a row before the resume point, the next ingest stores the parent’s final prompt and reply again without replay relations. This includes missing host state, missing parent or child records, a parent that did not end by compression or a fork marker; apparently complete ancestry also fails when an earlier process never wrote a needed predecessor record. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2463](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2463)).
- **A merged summary carrier creates an extra copy.** After the host merges LCM-X’s summary carrier into a user row, a warm replay from the start stores the merged carrier again, or stores copies from an otherwise unchanged view plus appended rows. Other middle-of-history edits do not belong to this limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1961](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1961)).
- **A restart of a long session can store hundreds of its rows again.** After a restart, a plugin reload or a new agent instance, the first ingest works out its resume point again from the store. When the stored rows no longer match the host's list in order, rows that reach LCM-X without a host timestamp are stored once more, with `observed_at` NULL. When Hermes's gateway rebuilds a conversation from its own database, only user turns keep their timestamp, so assistant replies and tool rows are the ones stored again. On the reference agent, the v0.30.0 field record showed hundreds of copies in one long session, with 475 and 487 at the two binds it could attribute individually. Nothing is lost: recall can return a row twice, and the store grows. v0.30.0 behaves the same way. On this release's install on the reference agent, the install, a forced restart and a plugin reload stored 11, 2 and 11 such copies, each of a row stored once before. Planned fix: v0.30.3, with a repair for existing copies ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **A rewritten unstamped view is stored again.** An ended engine’s final flush stores an unstamped view again after a resumed engine rewrites it, or a rewrite after a cold-start retry is stored again. A view with an additional host insertion or reordering is outside this limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2203](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2203)).
- **A message the host re-sends with a new message ID is stored again.** When the host sends a message it already sent, with the same text and timestamp but a new message ID, LCM-X stores a second identical row. v0.30.0 behaves the same way; this was not listed before. Which hosts give an unchanged message a new ID is not established ([#2720](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2720)).
- **An unanswered prompt becomes part of a composite.** After a restart before the reply, the unanswered prompt and the next prompt are stored together as a composite row beside the next prompt’s own row. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#849](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/849)).
- **Unstamped histories with existing copies grow on every restart.** On a host that sends no message timestamps, a session that already holds later exact copies of some rows stores its replayed history once more at each restart. Each extra copy has a possible-replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#588](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/588)).
- **Earlier ledger-off copies cannot anchor borrowed-timestamp links.** Borrowed-timestamp linking cannot see a copy stored while `LCM_INGEST_LEDGER` was off. It can therefore link to a different bound copy when complete bindings would have left the attribution ambiguous; no row or per-key count changes. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2443](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2443)).
- **A late tool call stores its result twice.** When a tool call's row was not stored at its turn, a later ingest that brings the call (typically after a restart or a rebind, when the host sends its full history) stores the call once and its result a second time, without a replay relation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2468](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2468)).
- **A persistent evidence fault can store the last row again.** After an evidence-read fault that persists past its retry (or a busy error followed by a one-off evidence-read fault, which gets no retry), the fail-open path can store the already-stored last row once more, shifted by a timestamped insert before it. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2374](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2374)).
- **Unstamped reply histories are stored again after an edit-and-resend and a restart.** On a host that sends replies without timestamps, a cold restart after an edit-and-resend stores the session's whole unstamped reply history again (41 copies after 40 turns in our test). From v0.30.1 each copy is linked to the stored reply with `possible_replay_of`, so the copies are visible, not silent; nothing is stored or skipped differently. Replies with host timestamps are not affected, and v0.29.1 and v0.29.2 store the same copies, without links. Pairing those replies within their turn is planned for a later v0.30.x patch ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479), [#2537](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2537)).
- **A new reply with the same text as an earlier reply can be marked as a possible copy.** After an edit-resend, when a cold restart links the reply copies it stores again, a genuinely new reply with the same text as an earlier reply can also be marked as a possible copy of it. The reply is stored and delivered as usual, and nothing hides or skips a row because of the mark ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479)).
- **A restart right after a fit-only compaction can save the summary again.** After a compaction that only trimmed the conversation to fit, if the host keeps the trimmed list and the agent restarts before LCM-X next saves the session, one extra copy of LCM-X's summary joined to the first kept message can be saved as a plain message. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2118](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2118)).
- **A to-do list merged with your next message can be saved again.** The host can merge a saved to-do list with your next message into one combined message. When that combined message splits cleanly into earlier saved messages of the same session, LCM-X now links it to them with `composite_of`. After a conversation ends and resumes, though, the combined message is saved again with no link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2488](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2488)).
- **A message can be saved twice after certain compaction passes.** After an overflow-recovery pass, or a compaction whose compacted messages were all hidden ones, if the host commits the rewritten conversation and restarts before the next compaction, a message can be saved again with no replay link. This has not been reproduced yet. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2134](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2134)).
- **A reused tool-call ID far apart can save a pair twice after a restart.** If a session reuses a tool-call ID for the same call and result more than 64 saved rows later, a restart can save that pair a second time without a replay link. No natural way to trigger this has been shown; our test forces it. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2197](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2197)).
- **A failed hand-off read can save a carried message again.** If LCM-X cannot read the previous session's record during a hand-off, a carried-over message can be saved again without a replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2490](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2490)).
- **A kept message with a model-switch note can be saved again.** After a compaction, when the conversation is picked up again, a kept message that starts with a model-switch note and is shown with an extra leading space can be saved again, along with the next carried-over message. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2431](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2431)).
- **Older databases without conversation IDs can save a tool pair twice.** On older databases with no conversation IDs recorded, a tool call and its result can be saved twice after a restart. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2436](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2436)).
- **An insert into a just-compacted conversation can save the latest reply again.** If the app inserts a message without a timestamp into a conversation that a compaction has just moved to a new session, and the latest reply also has no timestamp, LCM-X can save that reply a second time. Without the app's session database, the carried-over earlier prompts can be saved again too. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2491](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2491), [#2463](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2463)).
- **A few compaction and setting-change paths save a marked extra copy.** After certain compactions, a restart can save LCM-X's summary or the compacted input again, marked as a copy: when the compaction's saved record is out of date, when a compaction that moved the conversation to a new session (a non-default setting) is followed by a restart before the new session starts, or when a restart comes before a new compaction is adopted. Changing the redaction setting before LCM-X first saves a session with the ingest ledger on can also save one marked extra copy, once. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286), [#758](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/758)).
