- **A tool call with a long wrapped encoded block can be stored again.** A tool call whose arguments hold line-wrapped base64 of 4,096 characters or more, and its result, can be stored once more in four cases: at every cold restart on a store written before v0.30.0; after the host changed that call's arguments in place; when a session end after a restart or a rebind finds the database busy; and when the host re-sends the session's first message with a changed timestamp before a rebind. No row is lost; in the measurement in #2550, at most the first extra copy was linked as a possible replay, and the other copies were not marked. No supported Hermes version is known to change a stored call's arguments or to re-send an earlier message with a new timestamp. The first two cases also occur in v0.29.2, and all four in v0.30.0. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2550](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2550)).
- **A busy final save can store a session's final reply twice.** If the save at session end finds the database busy, LCM-X keeps that end's new rows for a retry. When a later save stores the final reply first and treats an earlier kept row differently (for example the long wrapped encoded block above), the retry stores the final reply again. Nothing is lost. It also occurs in v0.30.0. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2742](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2742)).
- A restart between in-turn compaction and the next save can leave a second stored copy of the turn's original request ([#3013](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3013)).
- If the same request already appears more than once in the compacted history, saving the turn after in-turn compaction can store the request again ([#3013](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3013)).
- If Hermes gives the restored request a different message UID when it writes it back, LCM-X can treat it as another user message ([#3013](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3013)).
- **One slow first turn after a restart on an affected session.** When one stored tool row carries only a name, the check at a cold start holds the store's write lock for about 4.3 s on a 2,000-row session in our measurement (an upper bound, taken on a shared machine). No data is affected. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2258](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2258)).
- **A crash after a compaction rotation, over ACP on upstream Hermes, can store one user turn twice.** The fault cells show it on both v0.30.0 and v0.30.1. Fix release not yet set ([#2507](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2507)).
- **After a crash during an upgrade from v0.27.0, a composite row is kept beside its replayed parts.** The fault cells show it on both v0.30.0 and v0.30.1 ([#1506](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1506)).
- **An equal-identity omission alignment can store a kept row twice.** This is the part of #1451 that stays open for v0.30.x ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)).
- **A compaction child resumed later by its own id is stored again.** If a compaction child whose rows v0.30.1 recovered is later resumed by its exact id without its conversation key (a CLI resume by the child's id, or a TUI lazy resume; not ACP or the gateway), it is bound into a new conversation and its whole list is stored there, copies of the recovered rows included. Nothing is lost ([#2630](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2630)).
- **Recovered rows can be stored out of order.** When the host later resumes a compaction child whose rows v0.30.1 recovered, and re-sends an earlier turn of that child with a changed timestamp or message ID, the recovered question and reply end up ahead of that re-sent turn in store order, instead of after it. Order only: the stored rows match v0.30.0's, with none lost or stored twice. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2672](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2672)).
- **After a restart, a system message the store never held makes one already-stored tool call and its result be stored a second time.** Nothing is lost: the extra rows repeat the same call and result. It happens when the host's first view after a restart starts with a system message that LCM-X never stored. v0.30.0 behaves the same way. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2852](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2852)).

Duplicate attribution requires the recorded ingest route and both store IDs; restart replay also requires the restart record. Timestamp absence alone does not establish a cause.

### Upgrades and saved tool results

- **Importing from lossless-claw again can store rows twice.** `scripts/import_lossless_claw.py` stores a row a second time when its source database has been moved or copied since an earlier import, or when the lines of a JSONL source without ids have shifted. Nothing is lost, and runtime ingest is not affected. Planned for a later v0.30.x patch ([#2739](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2739)).
- **Rolling back to v0.29.2 stores a saved tool result once more.** v0.30.0 stores the full content of a tool result that Hermes saved to a file. v0.29.2 knows such a result only as its short marker, so after a rollback it stores the tool call and the marker once more, the first time the host replays that history. Nothing is lost. The copy is not linked to the first one, and it does not grow on later replays or on upgrading again. Planned: link these copies on re-upgrade, in a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2552](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2552)).
- **A saved tool result that was stored as its marker stays a marker.** v0.29.2 stored a large tool result that Hermes had saved to a file as the short marker Hermes leaves in the conversation. After the upgrade, LCM-X keeps that row as it is and does not add the saved file's content. From v0.30.1 this also holds for the upgrade cases that v0.30.0 stored a second time (see **Changes since v0.30.0**), apart from the copy listed below. The same holds for a result whose file was missing when v0.30.0 first stored it, for one whose payload file LCM-X could not write then, and, with sensitive-pattern redaction on, for a result saved under Hermes's home whose preview held text that redaction rewrites: the row stays a marker afterwards. The marker and its preview are what the model was shown; nothing the host sent is lost. Other results whose file is present when v0.30.0 stores them are stored in full ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **A reused call ID with an identical marker can be stored once more.** If a host reuses a tool call ID and repeats the identical saved-output marker, and the store holds that marker as a marker (see the item above), a replay that starts at a different point in the history stores one more copy of it. This happens once; a later replay adds nothing, and no host row is lost. No supported Hermes version is known to reuse a call ID this way ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **After an upgrade from v0.29.2, a saved tool result can be stored once more when the host reuses its call id.** After an upgrade from v0.29.2, a tool call whose result is stored as a bare saved-output marker can be stored once more when the host later reuses that call id with the identical marker. v0.30.0 already stores the same copy at the first replay; v0.30.1 stores it at a later replay and never holds more rows than v0.30.0. Nothing is lost ([#2558](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2558)).
- **After an upgrade from v0.29.2, a replayed tool result sent as one text part can still be stored a second time** when v0.29.2 stored its saved-output marker bare. Nothing is lost. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch ([#2521](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2521)).
- **A store read error during an ingest can store a v0.29.2-era tool output twice.** If the store fails the one read that matches a replayed saved-output marker with the bare marker v0.29.2 stored, v0.30.1 stores the tool row again; v0.30.0 failed that ingest instead. We know no way to cause this read error in normal operation, because the read runs inside the ingest's write lock. Nothing is lost. Fix planned for a later v0.30.x patch ([#2701](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2701)).
- **A v0.29.2-era saved tool result can be stored again when its turn is replayed.** v0.29.2 stored some temporary saved-output markers as the recovered output, not as the marker. When the host replays such a turn after the upgrade and the saved temporary file is gone, LCM-X stores that tool result again: 3 or 4 extra rows over eight replayed turns in our tests. While the file is still there, nothing is stored twice. No row is lost, and v0.30.0 has the same behaviour. Fix planned for a later v0.30.x patch ([#2703](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2703)).
- **A helper agent's saved tool result can be stored one extra time.** LCM-X normally recognises a saved tool result by its marker. When a helper agent's history no longer lines up with its stored rows (the host trimmed or rewrote it, or after the helper agent's own compaction), LCM-X matches rows by counting them and compares the result's content instead. There, a result whose saved file is missing or was rewritten, or a reused tool call ID, is stored one extra time in total. No row is lost ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **A helper agent's row with an inline encoded block is stored more than once.** When a delegated helper agent's tool call holds an inline encoded block in its arguments, or a list-form row holds one in its content, LCM-X moves the block out when it stores the row, and at the next handover the stored row no longer matches what the host sends. The row is then stored again: one extra copy in a live helper session and at its end, up to two where rows are matched by counting, and up to three after the helper agent's own compaction. The copies stop after the second handover, and no row is lost. v0.29.2 does not store helper-agent sessions at all. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2559](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2559)).
- **With redaction on, a saved tool result whose preview holds redacted text is kept as its marker, and its conversation can be stored again after a restart.** Sensitive-pattern redaction is off by default. With it on, a tool result saved under Hermes's home whose preview holds text that redaction rewrites is stored as its marker: LCM-X keeps the marker and its preview, not the saved file's full text. When the preview ends inside a secret, a first part of it that is too short for a pattern to match stays in the stored preview. On a replay after a restart whose assistant and tool rows carry no timestamps, rows of that conversation can then be stored again, at each such replay; v0.29.2 stores the same rows or more. A replay that carries timestamps on every row stores nothing twice, except when the rewritten text is a password, which redaction replaces without keeping a fingerprint, and the replay sends only part of the history; rows are then stored again, fewer than in v0.29.2. No row is lost. v0.29.2 also keeps only the marker and its preview, with the same short first part. A store that the release candidates rc1 to rc5 wrote with redaction on has two more effects, described under **Upgrade** in the v0.30.0 notes. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604)).
- **While LCM-X cannot write its payload files, a replayed conversation that holds a saved tool result can be stored again.** If payload files cannot be written for a longer time (a full disk, or a payload folder that cannot be written to) while the database stays writable, a replay after a restart that sends only part of the history, and whose assistant and tool rows carry no timestamps, stores rows of such a conversation again at each replay, as v0.29.2 does. After the fault clears, a replay that sends only part of the history stores rows once more, and only once: with timestamps on every row, the tool call and its result, or the result alone when the replay starts at the result; without timestamps on assistant and tool rows, three rows, or two when the replay starts at the result. For a result under Hermes's home, v0.29.2 stores nothing again in the first case and stores rows again at every replay in the second. No row is lost ([#2605](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2605)).
- **A conversation stored with payload externalization turned off can be stored again on a replay.** Payload externalization is on by default. For a conversation that was stored with it off and holds a saved tool result, a replay after a restart stores rows of it again in 7 of the 12 replay forms tested: 5 with it still off, and 2 after it was turned on again. The copies can grow with each replay. No row is lost. v0.29.2 stores the same or more in every form. Tracked in [#2597](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2597).

### Search and recall

- **If your cloud embedding privacy policy changes on upgrade, semantic search over older summaries is partial until they are re-embedded.** The new policy changes the vector identity, so existing summary vectors stop counting until each summary is re-embedded. Publishing a leaf summary or binding a session schedules a catch-up pass under the configured batch limit, which defaults to 32. A pass can re-embed fewer summaries or skip the batch. On the reference agent, semantic search covered about 544 of 4,787 older summaries at release. Keyword and full-text recall are unaffected, and no stored row is lost. To finish sooner, run `/lcm embed backfill --corpus summary --apply` while the conversation is idle.
- **`lcm_grep` searches only the first 512 KB of a saved tool output.** The rest of the file is kept but is not searched. Fix release not yet set ([#2518](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2518)).
- **A value that appears only in a tool call's input is not searchable.** The call is stored, but search does not find a value that appears only in its arguments. Fix release not yet set ([#2519](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2519)).
- **In a saved tool output, `lcm_grep` finds a query only where it appears word for word.** A quoted phrase, the same words in another order or one extra word finds nothing in a saved tool output, although message search matches such queries term by term. In the read-only MCP reader, hybrid and semantic modes do not search saved tool outputs in the default scope (an explicit `content_scope` is served by full-text search); use `mode='full_text'` there. The first part is fixed on main ([#2586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2586), [PR #2587](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2587)); the second is tracked in [#2592](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2592), with no fix release set yet.

### Hosts and settings

- **On older Hermes hosts the long-turn recovery is off.** Hermes v0.21.6 and later include the post-tool re-anchor. LCM-X checks whether the host's `compress_after_tool_results` takes `current_turn_user_idx`. When it does not, LCM-X neither reports progress nor clears the host's two post-compaction flags, as in v0.30.0: the small-window long-turn recovery is off, and the host's post-tool, idle and cache-edge checks stay off after the first compaction. The other changes in this release still apply. Updating Hermes enables the recovery ([#2863](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2863)).
- **If LCM-X cannot read that capability, the recovery is off for the whole process even on a host that has the re-anchor, and no log line says so** ([#3013](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3013)).
- **The default large-output folder can ignore `HERMES_HOME`.** The checkout's git status probe can leave an empty lock file.
- **The next-stage message classifier has six correctness defects.** They are to be fixed before it is wired into ingest; no path reaches them today ([#2288](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2288)).
- **Some excluded parents still have stored children.** After an excluded parent rotates through compression, its delegated child is refused only on the shared route. Clone and prototype routes store the child despite `LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS` or the stateless exclusion patterns. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2070](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2070)).
- **The opt-in event recorder can keep one database file open until cleanup.** When the recorder replaces its database connection or hits a read error, it drops the old connection without closing it, so the file handle stays open until Python’s garbage collection runs. No data is affected. The recorder is off by default. Planned fix: a later v0.30.x patch, moved from v0.30.1 ([#2642](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2642)).

## Qualification

The v0.30.1 qualification evidence is bound to v0.30.1-rc4 (`c62f3b124280dd669a28cc61f90fd33035787262`). Its code is the frozen product commit `717a890e6df778b83cbf558a745f1d15ba4dcbe7`, with a release-notes-only change at the tag. The earlier carry decision was limited to rc3. On 2026-11-21, the release manager and owner agreed to limit GA to data safety (T1-459, spec row 942) after the L1 results and before reading any L2 or gate-copy result. T1-465 governs L2 faults. A real failure holds GA. A harness fault voids the attempt and triggers one rerun. Once all other GA checks pass, any row still running is read after GA. A real failure found then requires a same-day P0 patch. Phase B, Phase C, D5-B and the scoped reference-agent gate supply the remaining data-safety evidence under spec rows 941–942. Cloud-embedding recall after the privacy change was not re-measured for this release.

A scorecard cell is empty when this release has no gate result for that objective.

## Corrections after release (2026-11-22)

The text above is as published with the v0.30.1 tag. These corrections were accepted in review of the notes after the tag.

- **Rollback and the schema.** Under **Upgrade**, the **Rollback** bullet says "The schema does not change". More exactly: the store schema version stays 5. v0.30.1 adds the partial index `idx_msg_session_tool_call` on rows that carry a tool call id. The index stays after a rollback, and v0.30.0 reads and writes such a store. `test_v0300_forward_and_rollback_with_tool_call_index` in `tests/compat/test_tool_call_index_migration.py` checks this at the tag.
- **The v0.30.3 clause.** Under **Known issues**, the compaction item says the fix is planned for "v0.30.3, the release after the first patch release". v0.30.1 is itself the first patch release, so read it as "v0.30.3, after the v0.30.2 merged-reply fix".
- **Spec rows.** **Qualification** cites spec rows 936–942. They are not in the spec file on the release tree. They are at [`bench/specs/RELEASE-READINESS-V1.md` lines 936–942 at commit `d6a320c`](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/blob/d6a320c0d2c0d806de1e089b3cf649da0f0d57dc/bench/specs/RELEASE-READINESS-V1.md?plain=1#L936-L942).
- **Scorecard receipts and claim classes.** Each filled scorecard cell, with its receipts and its claim class:
  - Kept in store: [C1A-RECEIPT.md](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.30.1/C1A-RECEIPT.md), [PHASE-C-RECEIPT.md](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.30.1/PHASE-C-RECEIPT.md), [D5B-RECEIPT.md](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.30.1/D5B-RECEIPT.md) and [REFERENCE-GATE.md](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.30.1/REFERENCE-GATE.md). Claim class: bench lossless rows on the pinned rc4 tree plus one live profile's install.
  - Used correctly: [L1-RECEIPT.md](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.30.1/L1-RECEIPT.md). Claim class: L1 smoke tripwires only (D1 OFF, D4 mini).

- **Cloud rerank and the privacy setting.** `LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED` also governs the query and the candidate snippets that optional cloud rerank (`LCM_RERANK_ENABLED=true`, Voyage only, off by default) sends to Voyage. The privacy transform is off by default, so they are sent as stored unless it is `true`.
